sentences.text: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, a 7.3% CAGR [D5][D206].
Net income compounded at 9.7% and diluted EPS at 13.9% over the same window [F113][F115].
The shape is a step change rather than a smooth compound: revenue was $121.6 billion in FY2021, $128.7 billion in FY2022 and $158 billion in FY2023 [D110][D134][D159].
The FY2023 jump of 22.9% was driven by higher net interest income due to higher rates, partially offset by lower average deposit balances [D179][P36].
North America remains the concentration, at 76.6% of revenue in FY2025, but contributed only 0.2pp of the 2.8% revenue growth that year [D249][D251][D226].
Asia-Pacific grew 17.3% and contributed 1.2pp, and EMEA grew 9.5% and contributed 1.2pp in FY2025 [D300][D301][D275][D276].

Net interest income of $95.4 billion rose 3%, driven by higher Markets net interest income, higher revolving balances in Card Services and higher wholesale deposit balances, largely offset by deposit margin compression [F10][D221][P28].
Operating costs grew 1.4pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 4.2% [D225][D226].
EPS grew 1.4% against a 2.6% decline in net income, as the diluted share count fell 3.4% [D216][D214][D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, below the 57.2% window median and above the 51.7% window low set in FY2024 [D207][D333][D331].
That is far below the 61.7% banks peer median, ranking in the 0th percentile of seven peers [D337][D336].

Noninterest expense of $95.6 billion rose 4%, driven by higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation and technology and marketing investment, partly offset by FDIC special assessment releases [X137][D225][P26].
The credit-loss provision rose to 7.8% of revenue in FY2025 from 6.0% in FY2024, above the 6.0% peer median [D208][D185][D341].
Net margin of 31.2% sat 21.2pp below the 52.4% efficiency ratio's complement, with the 21.4% effective tax rate and the provision the main gaps [D210][D207][D203][D208].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was -$147.8 billion in FY2025 against net income of $57.0 billion [F60][F30].
The outflow resulted from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, net loan originations and higher other assets, partly offset by net income and higher trading liabilities [P21].
Capital return is the better lens: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion were 84.6% of FY2025 net income [D205][F30].
Stock-based compensation of $3.6 billion was small against that capital return and grew 3.1% [X50][D223].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, above the 11.8% banks peer median and in the 100th percentile of seven peers [D213][D339][D338].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits, up from 55.0% in FY2024, as loans grew to $1.47 trillion and deposits to $2.56 trillion [D211][D188][X197][X207].
Loans increased $121.1 billion, predominantly from higher CIB Markets loans and securities-based lending in AWM on higher client demand [P4].
Buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion in FY2025 exceeded the $48.2 billion combined figure's prior-year level, and the diluted share count fell 3.4% [X102][X112][D205][D224].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, and differs by up to 0.10% [R1][F26][X16][F30][X20].
The gap is immaterial to levels but means the 10-K figure should be cited where precision matters [R1].
FY2020 pretax income and income tax were later restated to $35.8 billion and $6.7 billion against the $35.4 billion and $6.3 billion used here [R2][R3][X63][X73].
The restatement is small and does not change the FY2020 margin conclusion [R2][R3].
Criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion, or 3.4% of wholesale credit exposure, from $44.7 billion and 3.5% [P2].
The absolute increase, driven by downgrades and new commitments, bears watching against the 1.8% allowance coverage [P2][D212].
Whether the efficiency ratio holds below the 57.2% window median in the FY2026 10-K [D333].
Whether the credit-loss provision stays above the 6.0% peer median or falls back toward the 5.0% FY2022 level [D341][D136].
Whether loans as a share of deposits rise past the 57.3% FY2025 level or reverse toward the 55.0% FY2024 figure [D211][D188].
